$comment: HAIP readiness track (inji-conformance run --track haip): the OpenID4VCI 1.0 HAIP issuer plan against Inji Certify with the closest settings Inji Certify can serve. HAIP allows only the authorization code flow with client attestation, which Inji Certify (pre-authorized code, no authorization_endpoint, no client authentication) does not offer, so the plan is expected to fail; results carry gating: false and never change the exit code.

vci.$comment: The issuer identifier is an origin without a path, so the suite finds the metadata at <origin>/.well-known/openid-credential-issuer. The configuration id is the one 'inji-conformance seed certify' creates.

client.$comment: Inji Certify does not authenticate clients at its token endpoint (Pre_Authorized_Code.md, limitation 1); the suite still signs a client assertion with this run-time key.

client2.$comment: Second wallet client of the multiple-clients module.

mtls.$comment: Client certificate from pki-init. Used when sender_constrain=mtls (the access token is bound to this certificate); the TLS proxy asks for it with ssl_verify_client optional_no_ca.

credential_configuration.$comment: Body of POST /v1/certify/credential-configurations. vcTemplate is written as JSON here; the runner sends it base64-encoded as Certify requires. The vct is a URN, so the suite does not try to fetch SD-JWT VC type metadata for it. Key ids and algorithm as in the upstream api-testrig's dc+sd-jwt case (AddCredentialConfigurationSd_Jwt.yml).

credential_offer.$comment: Body of POST /v1/certify/pre-authorized-data for every offer; the claims must match the configuration's claims. Each offer carries a new random numeric transaction code that the responder sends to the suite's tx_code_endpoint.
